pr_title: Improvements to SplitContainer including a drag bar background StyleBox
pr_body:
Improves `SplitContainer` in a number of ways making it much easier to script, and tidies up the code as follows:

- A new `split_bar_background` `StyleBox` allows solid color, gradients or textures to fill in the split bar behind or in place of the grabber icon.
- An essential new property `drag_area_scrollbar_offset` is required if one of the child controls has a scrollbar or other selectable control up against the split bar, in order to prevent the drag area from blocking mouse selection of the scroll bar or control.
- New signals `drag_started` and `drag_released` make it easier to script saving and restoring the `split_offset`
- A new property `dragging_enabled` separates dragging from `dragger_visibility` so the appearance of the drag bar is independent from whether dragging is enabled or not.
- A new method `get_drag_area_control` returns the `Control` so buttons or any other type of `Control` can ride along with the split bar (see demo video below).
- New properties `drag_area_margin_begin` and `drag_area_margin_end` allow for scripting the long-axis size of the drag area and background, which makes some nice uses like drawers simple to script (see video below).
- A new `drag_area_highlight_in_editor` property allows you to see the drag area during development.

<del>- A new virtual method `_splits_ready()` with a corresponding signal so a script knows when the split container children have been resized after the initial sort. This was a big problem because formerly, `SplitContainer._ready()` was called before the children had been fit to the container, and there was no easy way to get that information.</del>

This PR also fixes this issue and adds the theme fix: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/71862  and https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/71861

Adds this enhancement https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/61534

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/33969780/216680051-759ef971-ccf9-4601-a3d6-096fac0a4939.mov

This is all the GDScript neccessary for the buttons:
```
func _ready():
	var button := $Button
	var button_right := $ButtonRight
	remove_child(button)
	remove_child(button_right)
	hsplit.get_drag_area_control().add_child(button)
	hsplit.get_drag_area_control().add_child(button_right)
	button.position.y = -150 
	button_right.position.y = -50
```
https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/33969780/216681485-67b85ff1-5e9f-4876-816f-30a5ecb51ba8.mov


https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/33969780/216682037-9279d71b-3014-4049-a2cc-19ae316425ae.mov

Here's the editor with the drag areas visible:

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/33969780/216685254-c85713c1-e70b-4a71-8698-8932742ba855.mov

_Production edit:_ Closes https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/61534, closes https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/6230 and closes https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/6231.
pr_comments: That's a lot. It needs a proposal, or several, to explain various enhancements. Probably better done as several PRs too, but that would be more obvious after the proposals.

Okay. I’ll put the proposal together and follow up as necessary.

> On Feb 3, 2023, at 2:13 PM, Yuri Sizov ***@***.***> wrote:
> 
> 
> That's a lot. It needs a proposal, or several, to explain various enhancements. Probably better done as several PRs too, but that would be more obvious after the proposals.

> You are receiving this because you authored the thread.
>

Needs rebase.

> A new virtual method _splits_ready() with a corresponding signal so a script knows when the split container children have been resized after the initial sort.

You can also connect `sort_children` with CONNECT_DEFERRED and CONNECT_ONE_SHOT for the same result I think. Or `ready` with CONNECT_DEFERRED.

> You can also connect `sort_children` with CONNECT_DEFERRED and CONNECT_ONE_SHOT for the same result I think. Or `ready` with CONNECT_DEFERRED.

I just tried these, and `sort_children` emits too early, but `ready` with CONNECT_DEFERRED seems to work. The problem I was trying to solve invloves child `Controls` that are expensive to fit, which unpredictably cause `SplitContainer` `_ready()' to be called too early.

If there are still issues with the `ready` approach I will eventually know about it, so I could remove the proposed `_splits_ready()` and accompanying signal from the PR and put a new PR together later if an ugly head arises?

> If there are still issues with the ready approach I will eventually know about it, so I could remove the proposed _splits_ready() and accompanying signal from the PR and put a new PR together later if an ugly head arises?

Yeah right now the signal is not needed for anything. It's also inconsistent with other containers which don't expose anything like this.
This push included a rebase and removed the `_splits_ready()` virtual method and related signal.

> An essential new property drag_area_scrollbar_offset is required if one of the child controls has a scrollbar or other selectable control up against the split bar, in order to prevent the drag area from blocking mouse selection of the scroll bar or control.

Can you show an example when this is useful? The child nodes of SplitContainer can't be shrunk past their minimum size, so it's impossible to overlap scrollbars and drag area.

> New signals drag_started and drag_released make it easier to script saving and restoring the split_offset

Isn't `dragged` signal enough?

> New properties drag_area_margin_begin and drag_area_margin_end allow for scripting the long-axis size of the drag area and background, which makes some nice uses like drawers simple to script (see video below).

Which video?

> A new drag_area_show_drag_area property allows you to see the drag area during development.

Shouldn't this be editor-only? Also the double `drag_area` in name is awkward.

Disabling `dragging_enabled` makes the split area frozen:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/2223172/27125b3e-7aaf-49f8-ba9b-cdccba483227

At runtime it's at wrong position, different than in the editor.

> Can you show an example when this is useful? The child nodes of SplitContainer can't be shrunk past their minimum size, so it's impossible to overlap scrollbars and drag area.

Here's an exaggerated example with a `minimum_grab_thickness` of 50px and a separation of 1 with the grabber hidden. The first one has `drag_area_scrollbar_offset` set to `0`. The drag area is covering the `TextEdit` scrollbar so you can't interact with it using the mouse. A typical desired grab thickness is around 13px, whereas a dragger is often around 7px, so it gets covered.

The second video has `drag_area_scrollbar_offset` set to 25px, which shifts the drag area off the scroll bar. This is of course exaggerated and with a grab thickness of 13px, a shift of 5px works well to give both an easy-to-grab area, and access to the scrollbar.

The greenish areas are from turning on `show_drag_area`.

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/33969780/84f9d350-af5c-460d-967e-1cb12803fcc0

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/33969780/dc47f51a-fd9f-47db-a6d0-1fbdb9d36b1d

Hmm I suppose it makes sense 🤔
But are the exaggerated examples supported by some real use-cases?

> Isn't `dragged` signal enough?

`dragged` emits the offset `int` continuously, so you should use de-bouncers for every `SplitContainer` you were trying to handle at release or start, which gets extremely clumsy with lots of `SplitContainers`. You could argue the start and release are convenience signals, but they are like one short line of code each and make life very much better.

> But are the exaggerated examples supported by some real use-cases?

I wind up needing the shift for almost every `SplitContainer, both vertical and horizontal. I can show you the same example with the real-life sizes if you want to see that.

> Which video?

Here's the video. The drawer is made from three `SplitContainers`, the two horizontal ones that define the sides having their grabber area shortened using `drag_area_margin_end` to fit the middle vertical container. Very simple to script.

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/33969780/216682037-9279d71b-3014-4049-a2cc-19ae316425ae.mov

> But are the exaggerated examples supported by some real use-cases?

Here's a typical configuration: 13px wide drag area offset by 5px. Dragger is hidden and separation is zero.


https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/33969780/e8e05829-4232-4a09-821c-030cfbb3c8a9

> Shouldn't this be editor-only? Also the double `drag_area` in name is awkward.

You're sure right about the awkward double `drag_area` - should it be `drag_area_show`?

I think it's primarily useful for a user laying out an interface, because they don't have to attach a script to each `SplitContainer` to shade the grabber area while figuring out the best drag area width and offset.

You could argue that with `get_drag_area_control` you can easily script shading the drag area as needed, so if you advise I can remove `drag_area_show`.

> The drawer is made from three SplitContainers, the two horizontal ones that define the sides having their grabber area shortened using drag_area_margin_end to fit the middle vertical container. Very simple to script.

Could you share the scene? 👀

> You could argue that with get_drag_area_control you can easily script shading the drag area as needed, so if you advise I can remove drag_area_show.

No, I mean that the drag area shouldn't draw at runtime. Unless it has use outside the editor?

> No, I mean that the drag area shouldn't draw at runtime. Unless it has use outside the editor?

Oh, okay. Correct, it is not indended to draw at runtime. What is the recomended test for detecting runtime, not in the editor?
`Engine::get_singleton()->is_editor_hint()`

> Could you share the scene? 👀

Try this out:

[pull_down_drawer_example.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/11559827/pull_down_drawer_example.zip)

> Disabling `dragging_enabled` makes the split area frozen:

I'll fix this and make the other changes...

This push fixes the frozen split area and incorporates all the other change suggestions. It also fixes a bug where the icon was following the drag area, not the split display area, and now prevents `separation` values less than 0.

The drag area highlight color is now set to red if `dragging_enabled` is set to false, and does not draw at runtime as we discussed.


https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/33969780/8ebbb796-8ebb-48a3-91e2-790af5546e80

This push removed `DRAGGER_HIDDEN_USE_SEPARATION` and added notes to the documentation regarding the empty `ImageTexture` workaround for hairline split separations. Also a few small code tweaks and other doc improvements.

The prior push had also replaced all occurances of `get_theme_constant(SNAME("autohide"))` with `theme_cache.autohide`.

> I left some comments that should be addressed, but the added functionality works fine. 

Just pushed the changes per your last comments - thank you for all the excellent feedback!

> Approving the implementation; most of the additions don't seem to have linked proposals though.

There are two linked proposals that have all the additions and that this PR closes: [#6230](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/6230) and [#6231](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/6231)

> A new virtual method _splits_ready() with a corresponding signal so a script knows when the split container children have been resized after the initial sort. This was a big problem because formerly, SplitContainer._ready() was called before the children had been fit to the container, and there was no easy way to get that information.

See also https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/76349#issuecomment-1576967395.
Rebased to 4.2dev5.
@AThousandShips I'm not familiar with the doc classes error that occured with the last push - can you advise on the correct remedy? Thanks!

Some theme properties were recently moved from HSplitContainer and VSplitContainer to SplitContainer. You seem to have added them back. Run doctool and check if the generated XML includes all properties you have added.

So there are conflicts to resolve even though there is no difference between the two doc files.

Is there a way to simply remove those docs from the PR, or how do you resolve the conflict?
If you rebase you should see an option to resolve conflicts.

I was thinking about removing the SplitContainerDragger node as a whole and having its behaviors built into the SplitContainer. This would help with performance, since the control doesn't seem to be used for spacing whatsoever, only to draw and detect mouse entering/exiting.

But with the added functionalities, I guess it makes more sense to keep it as a control. I'm saying this because once you expose API for fetching the control, it will be more-or-less impossible to do what I thought of.

Can this be merged now into 4.3?

This PR makes the `SplitContainer` code easier to maintain and modify, and IMO should be merged prior to any of the other split container PR's, as it will simplify how those PR's can be implemented.
@kitbdev All the changes we discussed were made - thanks for the excellent suggestions!

Sorry for the delay following up.
We're now in feature freeze for 4.3, so I'm moving this to the 4.4 milestone. My understanding is that it's ready to go otherwise, so we can merge early on in the 4.4 dev cycle. It will need a rebase to solve present merge conflicts.

> We're now in feature freeze for 4.3, so I'm moving this to the 4.4 milestone. My understanding is that it's ready to go otherwise, so we can merge early on in the 4.4 dev cycle. It will need a rebase to solve present merge conflicts.

Sounds good. I will take care of the conflicts shortly.

In reference to #90411, there is quite a bit of overlapping effort (and similar thinking) in cleaning up `SplitContainer`, even before any additional features are implemented. Would it be easier to implement #90411 on top of this PR, since this PR addresses some more fundamental deficiencies? What is the sensible way to merge the efforts?

> In reference to #90411, there is quite a bit of overlapping effort (and similar thinking) in cleaning up `SplitContainer`, even before any additional features are implemented. Would it be easier to implement #90411 on top of this PR, since this PR addresses some more fundamental deficiencies? What is the sensible way to merge the efforts?

CC @kitbdev

I don't think there is much overlap in cleaning up SplitContainer, besides some minor doc issues. #90411 just needs to touch a lot of things due to logic changes. Where they do clean up, they clean up different things like `_get_sortable_child` `SortableVisbilityMode`, `#include`s, or `_get_separation()`. 

#90411 needs some fixes to properly handle changing child visibility, so it isn't ready yet, and I don't want to hold up other PRs. 
I don't mind rebasing on top of this. Though I would suggest some changes like moving draw back to the dragger.

> I don't think there is much overlap in cleaning up SplitContainer, besides some minor doc issues. #90411 just needs to touch a lot of things due to logic changes. Where they do clean up, they clean up different things like `_get_sortable_child` `SortableVisbilityMode`, `#include`s, or `_get_separation()`.
>
> #90411 needs some fixes to properly handle changing child visibility, so it isn't ready yet, and I don't want to hold up other PRs. I don't mind rebasing on top of this. Though I would suggest some changes like moving draw back to the dragger.

Thanks for offering to rebase on top of this. I did put the draw back into the dragger, and I see now why it needs to be there so you can have multiple dragger instances with more than two children. Each dragger now also saves its stylebox `Rect2`, so you should be able to keep an array of draggers and have them all update correctly. I believe the `SortableVisbilityMode` is also now there per a prior PR that hadn't yet been rebased here. Thanks for your comments, and I look forward to the multi-child improvements!
Thanks!

issue_context.title: Can't change color of splitcontainer
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

3.3.stable

### System information

Windows 10, GLES2, NVIDIA GTX 970

### Issue description

I've tried messing around with the theme options for the HSplitContainer, but I was unable to change the color of the divider. It's stuck to this plain gray.

### Steps to reproduce

Create a HSplitContainer and try to change the divider's color.

### Minimal reproduction project

_No response_
comments:
Having a divider modulate theme option for SplitContainer would be nice to have.

As a workaround, you can either color the image used for the divider or change the `self_modulate` property to color it.
I don't understand the issue, why is using `modulate` or `self_modulate` the workaround rather than the exact solution?
@Mickeon Most Control nodes that display images (like Button, ItemList, etc.) have a theme color for modulating the image only, but SplitContainer doesn't.
I was trying to implement this but I am struggling to even have a SplitContainer show its image on master...

review_comments: Maybe these should be theme items, since they also affect the background size?
These are convenient to modify while dragging, and can change during user input, so I think they are a better fit as properties.
This shouldn't really be exposed to scripting. It would make more sense as a button in the toolbar in a plugin.
Is there a way to show the property in the inspector, and hide it from scripting? I agree there's no need to expose it to scripting, but there's also no harm in it?
If we ever want to remove it in the future, it will be compatibility breaking. I don't know a better way to do it though.

If dragging is disabled while it is being dragged, it doesn't end properly and can cause issues next time it is enabled.

Also the mouse cursor isn't updated if its hovering it, you might need to call Viewport's `update_mouse_cursor_state` or something.
I had not anticipated disabling while dragging, so let me have a look at handling that correctly...
I tested the new push disabling while dragging, and the mouse cursor updates correctly.

Disabling while dragging works well now.
When I test it the mouse cursor doesn't update until it is next moved. It doesn't have to be dragging, just when the mouse is hovering the split bar and the disable state changes, the cursor should be updated.

I'm trying variations on the below and the cursor won't update until movement. Is there another class I can examine that has the behavior of updating the cursor while hovering and stationary after a state changes? What about using an `InputEventMouse` to trigger the update?
```
dragging_area_control->get_viewport()->update_mouse_cursor_state();
```

Hmm, that should work. `update_mouse_cursor_state` is what `set_default_cursor_shape` uses to update it immediately.
It uses an `InputEventMouseMotion` internally.
I guess if it isn't working then it can be looked into later.

Yes, I could not get that to work. Check out this new push and see if it does the trick. I'm also using an `InputEventMouseMotion` to cause a jiggle. I think it updates correctly when dragging and also when hovering.
Okay, I put in the viewport call that we can revisit later. Should be good for now.
